JSON: Name: reconnab_multimer_platform Title: Design and preclinical evaluation of Fab-anchored catalytically inactive ACE2 multimers for broad neutralization of ACE2-tropic betacoronaviruses Short Hypothesis: Fusing a highly conserved S2-binding non-neutralizing Fab to a catalytically inactive ACE2 and a multimerization domain increases neutralization potency and breadth against ACE2-tropic betacoronaviruses compared with equivalent multimeric ACE2 constructs lacking the Fab anchor. Related Work: Approved and investigational SARS-CoV-2 monoclonal antibodies have targeted RBD epitopes and lost clinical efficacy when viral RBDs mutated; S2-directed antibodies recognize more conserved regions but typically exhibit weak neutralization. Engineered ACE2 decoys and ACE2-Fc fusions broaden target range by competing for receptor binding and have shown in vitro and some in vivo activity, but many designs introduce affinity-enhancing ACE2 mutations that could alter escape dynamics and several constructs have limited in vivo potency or half-life. Multimerization of ACE2 increases avidity and neutralization potency in multiple reports, yet multimeric ACE2 constructs vary in domain architecture and often lack Fc effector functions or exhibit rapid clearance. Existing gaps include: (1) combining conserved-epitope anchoring with receptor decoys to improve local effective ACE2 concentration has not been systematically compared to ACE2 multimers alone; (2) trade-offs among expression yield, stability, and in vivo half-life for tri-component fusion proteins are unresolved; and (3) the contribution of Fc-mediated effector functions and ACE2 catalytic activity to efficacy and safety remains under-characterized. Abstract: Rapid viral evolution of ACE2-tropic betacoronaviruses undermines monoclonal antibody efficacy that targets variable RBD epitopes. We propose a modular therapeutic architecture that links a pan-betacoronavirus S2-binding Fab (anchor) to a catalytically inactive ACE2 receptor domain (neutralizer) and a multimerization module (avidity enhancer) to produce ReconnAb multimers. The design aims to (1) lock ACE2 neutralizers locally at conserved spike trimer interfaces via the Fab anchor, (2) increase effective ACE2 valency through dimeric or trimeric scaffolds, and (3) reduce off-target enzymatic activity by catalytic inactivation. Main contributions are: identification and use of a high-affinity cross-reactive S2 Fab as an anchoring module; demonstration that Fab-anchored iACE2 multimers achieve higher in vitro neutralization potency than multimeric iACE2 alone; and preclinical evaluation of pharmacokinetics and in vivo protection against an Omicron XBB.1.5 challenge. Expected outcomes include a validated candidate construct class with quantifiable potency and breadth against current and phylogenetically diverse ACE2-dependent betacoronaviruses and a defined preclinical dataset addressing half-life and safety-relevant parameters. Experiments: Constructs and reagents: (a) ReconnAb-dimer: CoV2-26 Fab — flexible linker — catalytically inactive human ACE2 (H345L) — human IgG1 Fc; (b) ReconnAb-trimer: CoV2-26 Fab — linker — iACE2 — cartilage matrix trimerization domain; (c) controls: iACE2-dimer (Fc-iACE2), iACE2-trimer, ReconnAb-dimer lacking Fab anchor, ReconnAb constructs with catalytically active ACE2 (WT), bebtelovimab, monomeric ACE2, and vehicle. In vitro neutralization panel: pseudoviruses bearing spike from SARS-CoV-2 variants in emergence order (Wuhan, Beta, Omicron BA.5, JN.1, BQ.1, XBB.1.5, XBB.2.3, EG.5.1) and phylogenetically distant ACE2-tropic betacoronaviruses (SARS-CoV, WIV1-CoV, PRD-0038, HKU5-CoV-2). Authentic virus neutralization: WA-1, Omicron BA.5, JN.1, XBB.1.5. Cell lines: HEK293T/ACE2/TMPRSS2, HeLa-ACE2/TMPRSS2, VeroE6-TMPRSS2-ACE2. Assays and metrics: binding kinetics (BLI): Kd, kon, koff; thermal stability (DSF): Tm; expression yield: mg protein/L; pseudovirus neutralization: IC50 and IC80 (non-linear four-parameter regression, n>=3 independent replicates); authentic virus neutralization: TCID50/PRNT50 IC50 (n>=3); Fc effector function assays: ADCP, ADCC, ADCD (percent activity relative to IgG control); pharmacokinetics: serum concentration by sandwich ELISA, calculate t1/2, Cmax, AUC (n>=5 mice per group); tissue distribution: organ concentrations (lung, kidney, spleen) at 24h; in vivo efficacy: AC70 hACE2 transgenic female mice challenged intranasally with XBB.1.5 at 1.96×10^4 PFU; groups (n=10 per group): vehicle, ReconnAb-dimer (10 mg/kg i.v. at 12h, 30h, 48h post-infection), ReconnAb-trimer (same dosing), iACE2-dimer (same); endpoints: survival (log-rank test), daily body weight, clinical scores, oral swab qRT-PCR viral RNA copies (days 1,2,3,5), lung viral titers at euthanasia (plaque assay). Ablation and comparisons: (1) Avidity effect: compare ReconnAb-dimer vs ReconnAb-trimer vs iACE2-dimer vs iACE2-trimer for IC50 and in vivo endpoints; (2) Anchor effect: compare ReconnAb-dimer vs identical construct with Fab removed to quantify fold-change in potency; (3) Catalysis effect: compare iACE2(H345L) vs iACE2(WT) versions for safety biomarkers (blood pressure, renal ACE2 activity) and efficacy; (4) Format effect: compare Fab-based vs scFv-based ReconnAb constructs for expression yield, Tm, and neutralization. Statistical analysis: IC50 comparisons via ANOVA with Tukey post-hoc; viral load comparisons via Mann-Whitney U; survival by log-rank; report mean±SEM and 95% CI. Success criteria: ≥10-fold improvement in IC50 over iACE2-dimer against multiple VOCs and significant survival benefit (p<0.05) in XBB.1.5 challenge. Risk Factors and Limitations: Technical failure modes: fusion constructs may misfold, aggregate, or have low expression yield at manufacturing scale; Fab anchoring may sterically block ACE2 binding in some spike conformations reducing potency. Pharmacokinetic constraints: ACE2 ectodomain may accelerate proteolytic cleavage or clearance leading to short in vivo half-life; LS Fc mutations may be insufficient to extend t1/2. Immunogenicity and safety: multi-domain human-derived fusions can elicit anti-drug antibodies; residual ACE2 activity or receptor engagement could perturb renin-angiotensin signaling despite catalytic inactivation; Fc effector functions may cause immunopathology or enhanced inflammation. Breadth limitation: method targets only ACE2-dependent betacoronaviruses and will not neutralize viruses that switch receptor usage or evolve to reduce Fab epitope accessibility via conformational masking. Viral escape risk: selection pressure could favor spike variants that alter trimeric-interface exposure or receptor-binding geometry without losing ACE2 usage. Evaluation biases: laboratory-grown isolates and pseudovirus panels may not capture full sequence diversity of circulating strains; small animal models may not predict human pharmacodynamics and safety. Scalability: complexity of tri-domain fusions may complicate GMP production, glycosylation heterogeneity, and formulation stability for clinical deployment.
